clue.text: What's guest primarily have to bring, loaded?

definitions.text: What's guest primarily have to bring, loaded?

indicators.note: loaded is slang for drunk, so the words before it reel into a new order
primarily asks for the first letter of the word guest

explanation.surface: A question about what a visiting guest is expected to arrive carrying, presumably laden with gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' shuffles HAVE TO BRING into OVERNIGHTBA, and 'primarily' adds G from guest at the end; the whole clue also describes what a guest staying over brings.
explanation.definitionFit: A holdall packed for a single night away is exactly what a staying visitor carries.

clue.text: Academic administrator failing opportunity with 24?

parts.note: a failing or moral weakness is a vice
an opportunity is a chance
the answer to 24 across read as an instruction: a word for a bread bun written upward, as it is in a down clue, gives these letters

explanation.surface: A university official's shortcomings are blamed on chance and a cross-reference.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is the trick: 24's answer, taken as an instruction, has the word ROLL turned upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: In British universities this officer is the working head, the chancellor being largely ceremonial.

clue.text: She has origins in really early Delta Dawn years

indicators.note: origins in asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A woman whose roots lie in the early dawn of the Mississippi delta.
explanation.walkthrough: Helen Reddy had a 1973 hit with the song 'Delta Dawn', so the surface quietly points at her.
explanation.definitionFit: The singer Helen Reddy is a woman, so the pronoun stands for her.

clue.text: What happens to make rani late with payments?

parts.note: the answer read as an instruction says the letters I N A R rear up, that is turn back, which spells this Indian queen's title

explanation.surface: An Indian queen asks what has made her fall behind with her bills.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, IN AR followed by 'rears', reverses those letters into RANI.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind with money owed is the standard idiom for overdue debt.

clue.text: Game focused on character selection and execution

definitions.text: Game focused on character selection and execution

parts.words: Game focused on character selection and execution
parts.note: a word-guessing pastime where players pick letters one at a time while a gallows drawing grows

explanation.surface: A game whose rules centre on picking characters and carrying out the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' means a letter of the alphabet, and 'execution' is a hanging, not the carrying out of a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: The pencil game has players choose letters, wrong guesses building a gallows picture.

clue.text: Cellist's country cottage?

parts.note: a musician who draws a bow across strings could be called by this word, which also means a leafy rural retreat

explanation.surface: Where a cello player might live out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means one who plays with a bow, such as a cellist, and also a shady rural dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old term for a rustic cottage or arbour and also, whimsically, a person using a bow.

clue.text: Chatter about wobbly 16 in upmarket boozer

indicators.note: about means one word surrounds the others

parts.note: to chatter is to gab
throwing a wobbly is British slang for a tantrum, also called a strop
16 across means high-class, which is also U, the old British label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: Talk about a shaky posh person in a smart pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wobbly' looks like an anagram signal but is a noun: a fit of temper. U for upper-class is a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang for a pub; this kind serves high-quality food.

clue.text: Whiter than white mutant obvious in space

indicators.note: a mutant is changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An obvious mutant floating in outer space is pale beyond pale.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe someone morally spotless, beyond any doubt of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Burning fossil fuels produces this carbon in top-rate exhaust

indicators.note: in means the carbon symbol sits inside

parts.note: top-rate is A1, written AI in crosswords
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
to exhaust is to drain

explanation.surface: A science note on fossil fuel combustion, carbon and top-rate exhaust fumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur and nitrogen oxides from combustion make precipitation acidic and harmful.

clue.text: Pungent green paste had versatile tastes

parts.note: someone with versatile tastes is a bi
someone with versatile tastes is a bi

explanation.surface: A sharp green condiment that apparently appealed to varied palates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'versatile tastes' hints at a bisexual, slang BI, so the phrase reads WAS A BI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese horseradish condiment is a hot green paste served with sushi.

clue.text: I'm skilled at divining whiskey in senior common room

indicators.note: in means the drink sits inside the abbreviation

parts.note: SCR is the abbreviation for a university senior common room
rye is an American whiskey

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller boasts while drinking whiskey among university dons.
explanation.walkthrough: The senior common room is the staff lounge in British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: A crystal-gazer foretells the future by peering into a glass or bowl.

clue.text: German nobleman's to do some damage in cemetery

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or do some damage
a grave is what is found in a cemetery

explanation.surface: A German aristocrat sets out to vandalise a graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the hereditary title of a count ruling a border province of the Holy Roman Empire.

clue.text: Someone advising caution about crooked regional employee

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the second

parts.note: a person who advises caution gives a warning
agee is a Scottish and northern dialect word for crooked or awry

explanation.surface: A cautious adviser talks of a dishonest employee from the provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regional' marks AGEE as a dialect word, not a geographical clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone paid a salary or weekly pay for work is a worker on payroll.

clue.text: Watched and heard two-tone horse, initially silent?

indicators.note: heard means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: a piebald is a two-tone horse; with its first letter silent it is pronounced like these letters

explanation.surface: Someone watched and listened to a patched horse that stood quiet at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the opening P of PIEBALD and what is said, IEBALD, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare hard at something is to look it over closely.

clue.text: About time detain a fool who supported former president

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: detain means one word holds the others inside

parts.note: an age is a period of time
nit is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Concerning time spent locking up an idiot who backed an ex-president.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Ronald Reagan, the fortieth US leader, backed his policies.

clue.text: High-class surgery rejected by small hospital

indicators.note: rejected means the word for surgery is sent back the other way

parts.note: an op is a surgical operation

explanation.surface: A smart clinic is turned down by a little hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart, upper-class and expensive are what the informal word conveys.

clue.text: Top marks received by champion

indicators.note: received by means the second piece is taken inside the first

parts.note: an ace is a champion or expert
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Full marks go to the champion.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or highest point of something is its summit.

clue.text: Busy dates arranged around new churchgoing habit

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation
arranged means these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A packed diary is reorganised round a new habit of going to church.
explanation.definitionFit: Habit can mean clothing, and this is the finest outfit kept for church on the Sabbath.

clue.text: North Surrey, criminal breeding-ground

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news line calling north Surrey a hotbed of crime.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county just south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where plants or young are raised, or where something grows, is a figurative breeding place.

clue.text: Inevitable ache readily exposes possible peroxide user

indicators.note: exposes means the letters are laid bare inside the run of words before it

explanation.surface: An unavoidable pain is easily revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who whitens hair or fabric might use hydrogen peroxide to do it.

clue.text: Overstimulated and vacant halfway through

indicators.note: vacant means the word is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: per means through or by way of

explanation.surface: Someone wired and blank-eyed halfway through something.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means excitable and overexcited, wound up.

clue.text: Reclines at three-quarter length, turning to make a descent

indicators.note: turning means the shortened phrase is read back to front
three-quarter length keeps six of the eight letters, cutting the last quarter

parts.note: to recline is to lie back

explanation.surface: Someone lounging at an angle turns over to climb down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at three-quarter length' trims LIESBACK to LIESBA, and 'turning' reverses that.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers go down a rock face on a doubled rope in a controlled descent.

clue.text: Was a Quaker to drive away king?

parts.note: to shoo is to drive away
K is the abbreviation for king in chess

explanation.surface: A question whether being a member of the Society of Friends meant driving a king away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quaker' looks like the religious group but just means one who quakes, or shakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Trembling with fear or cold is what a quaking person does.

clue.text: To arrive, haul sides of oar, facing the stern

indicators.note: facing the stern means looking backward, so the letters run back to front

parts.note: to haul is to pull

indicators.note: sides of asks for the first and last letters of oar

explanation.surface: A rower arrives, hauling on the oar while facing the back of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Rowers do face the stern, which hides that the phrase turns PULLOR round.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up somewhere, especially casually, is an informal idiom for coming.

clue.text: Broadcast is copied in several parts

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A programme that is transmitted is duplicated across several sections.
explanation.definitionFit: Something told in instalments or separate incidents is serialised.

clue.text: Short break not spent in Bath?

definitions.text: Short break not spent in Bath?

parts.words: Short break not spent in Bath?
parts.note: a brief illicit getaway that is anything but clean, Bath being a spa city famous for bathing

explanation.surface: A mini holiday taken somewhere other than the English spa city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city famous for its Roman baths; read as 'bath', the trip is unwashed.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit romantic getaway for two is a couple of nights away, often secret.
